title: Guide
intro: How to prepare a template, fill it from your data, and connect DocuMind AI to your own systems.

blocks.text: You have a document you send often (an offer, a contract, a change of terms) and a spreadsheet of people to send it to. DocuMind AI produces one for each row, keeping your letterhead, tables and formatting exactly as they are.
Your template decides the wording and your data decides the values. Every document is checked before it reaches anybody, and nothing can be downloaded until a person has approved it.

items.title: Create a project
items.text: A project is one document type for one purpose. Its templates, data and documents all live inside it.

items.title: Upload your template
items.text: Upload a `.docx`. Within moments you see how many values and optional sections were found, and anything that needs fixing before you go on.

items.title: Get the spreadsheet and fill it in
items.text: Download the data spreadsheet made for your template. It has one column per value, named after it, and a fixed list of choices on any column that decides which sections appear. Fill in one row per person and upload it.

items.title: Match the columns, then generate
items.text: Columns are matched to values for you; confirm them and start the batch. A few documents are checked first, and the rest continue once they pass.

items.title: Review, approve, download
items.text: Documents appear as they are produced. Move each through your own workflow, send any you disagree with to review, and approve the ones that are right. Only an approved document can be downloaded.

blocks.text: Every piece of text in your template is one of three things, and you say which by its font colour.

items.name: Blue: a value
items.means: Replaced with your data. Each blue item becomes one spreadsheet column.

items.name: Red: an instruction
items.means: A note for whoever prepares the document. Removed before sending.

blocks.text: Write a value as its name in angle brackets and colour it blue, for example `<Base Salary>`. Type each placeholder in one go: a placeholder whose formatting changes halfway through cannot be filled.
If your documents already use the highlighter instead of font colour, that works too.

blocks.title: Never draw a blank.
blocks.text: A gap written as `__/__/____` or `XX months` has nothing to attach data to, so it stays exactly as you typed it. Give it a name instead. One date is one placeholder, not three.
Text that should appear only sometimes goes between markers. Colour the markers red so they are removed either way.

[[IF employment_basis == 'Part Time']]
You will work on a part-time basis as set out in Schedule 1.
[[ELSE]]
You will work on a full-time basis.
[[ENDIF]]
`[[ELSE]]` is optional, and markers can sit inline within a sentence. What you can write in a condition:

rows: greater than, less than or equal to (also >= and <)

blocks.text: On the left, use the name of a blue value in lower case with underscores instead of spaces. Angle brackets are for values only, never for optional wording: a phrase like `<on a part time basis>` is a condition, not a value, and will be rejected.
A document carries two states at once, because they answer different questions.

items.title: Its review status
items.text: Draft, awaiting a decision, changes requested, failed checks, approved. Set by the checks and by reviewers, not by hand.

items.title: Where you have put it
items.text: Work in progress, completed, cancelled. Yours to set. Approved and blocked appear here too but cannot be chosen: one is a signature, the other a failed check.

blocks.title: Only an approved document can be downloaded.
blocks.text: This is enforced on every route, not just hidden in the interface.
Everything the interface does is available over HTTP. The base URL is your deployment followed by `/api/v1`.

# 1: get a token
curl -X POST https://your-host/api/v1/auth/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"you@example.com","password":"…"}'

# → {"access_token":"eyJ…","token_type":"bearer"}

# 2: use it on every call
curl https://your-host/api/v1/projects \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

blocks.title: Tokens expire.
blocks.text: Long jobs can outlive one, so request a fresh token per job rather than holding one for the life of a run.
Uploads are `multipart/form-data` with the file under the field name `file`. Everything else is JSON, and times are ISO 8601. Every response is scoped to your organisation.
Failures carry a stable code and a sentence written for a person.
Branch on `code`, never on the message: the wording improves over time, the code does not. The ones you can act on:

rows: Approve the document before downloading it.
The document failed its checks. Fix the data or template and generate it again.
The spreadsheet has headers but no data. Add rows and upload it again.
Your role cannot do this. Ask an administrator.
Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.
The item does not exist or belongs to another organisation.

blocks.text: Documents from your own system, start to finish. Each step waits for the one before, so check a batch's progress rather than assuming it has finished.

BASE=https://your-host/api/v1
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# 1: a project
PID=$(curl -s -X POST $BASE/projects -H "$AUTH" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Offer letters","region":"Asia Pacific",
       "function":"Human Resources","document_type":"HR Letters"}' | jq -r .id)

# 2: upload the template
TID=$(curl -s -X POST $BASE/projects/$PID/templates -H "$AUTH" \
  -F file=@offer-letter.docx | jq -r .id)
TV=$(curl -s $BASE/templates/$TID/manifests -H "$AUTH" | jq -r '.items[0].id')

# 3: the spreadsheet this template needs, then fill it in and upload it
curl -s $BASE/template-manifests/$TV/source-template -H "$AUTH" -o data.xlsx
#    … one row per person …
SV=$(curl -s -X POST $BASE/projects/$PID/sources -H "$AUTH" \
  -F file=@data.xlsx | jq -r .current_version_id)

# 4: match the columns and save
curl -s "$BASE/template-manifests/$TV/binding-suggestions?source_version_id=$SV" \
  -H "$AUTH" | jq '{source_version_id:"'$SV'",
      field_bindings:[.suggestions[]|select(.column)|{key:.field_id,value:.column}]|from_entries}' \
  > matches.json
curl -s -X POST $BASE/template-manifests/$TV/bindings -H "$AUTH" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @matches.json

# 5: generate, then wait for the batch
JOB=$(curl -s -X POST $BASE/template-manifests/$TV/generate-batch -H "$AUTH" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"source_version_id":"'$SV'","language":"en"}' | jq -r .job_id)
until [ "$(curl -s $BASE/jobs/$JOB -H "$AUTH" | jq -r .status)" != "running" ]; do sleep 2; done

# 6: approve, then download
for V in $(curl -s $BASE/projects/$PID/documents -H "$AUTH" | jq -r '.items[].current_version_id'); do
  curl -s -X POST $BASE/document-versions/$V:approve -H "$AUTH" > /dev/null
  curl -s "$BASE/document-versions/$V/download?format=docx" -H "$AUTH" -o "$V.docx"
done

blocks.title: Step 3 is worth keeping.
blocks.text: Using the spreadsheet made for your template means every column name matches a value exactly. With your own export, check the suggested matches before generating.
